paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Jesus did not come to throw out the Law and the Prophets. He says, "I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them" (Matthew 5:17). And He wants a righteousness that goes deeper than what the scribes and Pharisees showed (Matthew 5:20).

Notice where Jesus keeps digging. Again and again He says, "But I tell you," and He goes past what a person does to what is going on inside (Matthew 5:22, 28, 34, 39, 44). Anger, lust, a promise you don't mean, a grudge against an enemy: these start in the heart before they show up in the hands. I could stamp a cookie perfect on the outside and still have burnt dough in the middle, and that's how a heart can look when only the outside got cleaned up.

So what do you do with this, baker? Jesus ends with "Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect" (Matthew 5:48). He points to how the Father treats people, with sun on the evil and the good, and calls us to love like that, even our enemies (Matthew 5:44-45). That is a mountain-sized call, and Jesus is still teaching on that mountain, so the story isn't over.
